1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. This also occurs in verses 9, 12, and 13 of this chapter.

1.q: הָל֞וֹךְ וְ⁠קָנִ֤יתָ לְּ⁠ךָ֙ אֵז֣וֹר פִּשְׁתִּ֔ים וְ⁠שַׂמְתּ֖⁠וֹ עַל־מָתְנֶ֑י⁠ךָ
1.note: Buying a linen loincloth and putting it around his waist was a symbolic action by which Jeremiah showed how closely Yahweh had bound the people of Israel and Judah to himself. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Go and buy a linen loincloth for yourself and put it around your loins, to show how closely I have bound my people to myself]

A **linen loincloth** is a kind of undergarment made of cloth that a man wrapped around his waist and hips. If your readers would not be familiar with what a linen loincloth is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a cloth undergarment made of linen]

The implication is that Yahweh is telling Jeremiah not to wash the loincloth. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [but do not let it get wet by washing it]

2.note: See how you translated this expression in 8:9. This also occurs in verses 3 and 8 of this chapter.

3.note: Jeremiah is using **And the word of Yahweh was to me a second time** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh spoke to me again.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke to me again]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:4.

4.note: Yahweh is using **arise** as a common expression of the culture to mean “set out to do something.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and set out and go to Perath]

The word **Perath** is the name of a place that is also referred to in verses 5–7. It is the same word that elsewhere is translated as “Euphrates.” This could refer to: (1) a place where there is a stream, mentioned in Joshua 18:23 as Parah, about 5 and a half kilometers (3.5 miles) northeast of Anathoth, which is about that same distance northeast of Jerusalem. It seems likely that Jeremiah traveled to this nearby place with a name that sounded very much like “Euphrates,” which would symbolize for him that great river of Babylon. (2) the Euphrates River, about 550 kilometers (350 miles) from Anathoth. Alternate translation: [the Euphrates River]

6.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **And it happened from the end of many days** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Jeremiah is using **from the end of many days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “after a long time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [after a long time had passed]

7.note: Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his readers’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and look]

The expression **was ruined** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the loincloth had rotted away]

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:4.

9.q: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כָּ֠כָה אַשְׁחִ֞ית אֶת־גְּא֧וֹן יְהוּדָ֛ה
9.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that in this way he will ruin the majesty of Judah]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **majesty**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what makes Judah majestic and what makes Jerusalem so very majestic]

Here, **Judah** and **Jerusalem** represent “the people who live in those places.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the majesty of the people of Judah and the great majesty of the people living in Jerusalem]

10.q: הָ⁠עָם֩ הַ⁠זֶּ֨ה הָ⁠רָ֜ע הַֽ⁠מֵּאֲנִ֣ים לִ⁠שְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֗⁠י הַ⁠הֹֽלְכִים֙ בִּ⁠שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֔⁠ם וַ⁠יֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְ⁠עָבְדָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠הִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת לָ⁠הֶ֑ם וִ⁠יהִי֙ כָּ⁠אֵז֣וֹר הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
10.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what Yahweh will do to these people before the long description of who they are and what they have done. Alternate translation: [I will punish this evil people—the ones who refuse to listen to my words, the ones walking in the stubbornness of their heart, and they have walked after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. Let them be like this loincloth]

10.q: הָ⁠עָם֩ הַ⁠זֶּ֨ה הָ⁠רָ֜ע הַֽ⁠מֵּאֲנִ֣ים לִ⁠שְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֗⁠י הַ⁠הֹֽלְכִים֙ בִּ⁠שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֔⁠ם וַ⁠יֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְ⁠עָבְדָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠הִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת לָ⁠הֶ֑ם וִ⁠יהִי֙ כָּ⁠אֵז֣וֹר הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
10.note: In this verse, the word **people** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the people of Judah as a group, and Yahweh refers back to it with the singular pronoun **him**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “people” and a plural pronoun. Alternate translation: [These evil people … let them be like this loincloth]

The implication is that these people refuse to obey what Yahweh tells them, not merely that they refuse to hear it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the ones who refuse to obey my words]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the way these people live were **walking**, and as if what they are determined to do were the **stubbornness of their heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones living according to their own stubborn desires]
See how you translated this expression in 9:14.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if these people had **walked after other gods** when they served them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they have followed other gods]

Bowing down before an image was a symbolic action by which a person showed that he worshiped the god that the image represented. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and to bow down before their images to worship them]

10.q: וִ⁠יהִי֙ כָּ⁠אֵז֣וֹר הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יִצְלַ֖ח לַ⁠כֹּֽל
10.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **this loincloth** is **not good for anything**, so these people will be of no use to Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [let him become useless to me, just as this loincloth is not good for anything]

11.q: כִּ֡י כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ יִדְבַּ֨ק הָ⁠אֵז֜וֹר אֶל־מָתְנֵי־אִ֗ישׁ כֵּ֣ן הִדְבַּ֣קְתִּי אֵ֠לַ⁠י אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙
11.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a loincloth clings to the loins of a man**, so Yahweh bound the people of Israel and Judah closely to himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [For just as a loincloth stays tightly wrapped around a man’s waist, so I bound the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah closely to myself]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the loins of men]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if all the descendants of Israel and of Judah were a **house**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the descendants of Israel and all the descendants of Judah]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 14 and 25.

The terms **name**, **praise**, and **glory** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and be for my great renown]
Here, **name** represents reputation or renown. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and be for renown]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **praise** and **glory**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [and to praise me, and to honor me as glorious]

12.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because of that, you shall speak]

12.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּל־נֵ֖בֶל יִמָּ֣לֵא יָ֑יִן
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that Yahweh, the God of Israel, says that every jar shall be filled with wine]

The expression **shall be filled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [You must fill every jar with wine]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were jars that he would fill with **wine**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Every one of you will be filled with wine like a jar]

A **jar** is a kind of large clay container that people used for storing wine. If your readers would not be familiar with what a jar is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [Every large container for liquid]

12.q: הֲ⁠יָדֹ֨עַ֙ לֹ֣א נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כָל־נֵ֖בֶל יִמָּ֥לֵא יָֽיִן
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that they know very well that every jar will be filled with wine]

12.q: הֲ⁠יָדֹ֨עַ֙ לֹ֣א נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כָל־נֵ֖בֶל יִמָּ֥לֵא יָֽיִן
12.note: The people are using the question form to express scorn for what Jeremiah has told them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [We certainly know that every jar will be filled with wine!]

The people are repeating forms of the verb **know** in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Do we not know with certainty]

The expression **will be filled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people fill every jar with wine]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people will say to you, Jeremiah]

13.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְ⁠נִ֣י מְמַלֵּ֣א & וְ⁠אֶת & שִׁכָּרֽוֹן
13.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that he will fill with drunkenness]

Yahweh is using **Behold** with the participle that follows as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to do this.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to fill]

13.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְ⁠נִ֣י מְמַלֵּ֣א אֶת־כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָ⁠אָ֪רֶץ הַ⁠זֹּ֟את & שִׁכָּרֽוֹן
13.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the helplessness that he will bring on the people of this land were **drunkenness** with which he would fill them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says, “I am about to make all of the ones inhabiting this land completely helpless]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **drunkenness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the appearance that they are drunk]

Here, **throne** represents royal authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the ones exercising royal authority]

14.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people were jars that he would **smash** against one another. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will destroy each man along with his brother]
See how you translated this expression in 6:21.

The terms **pity**, **spare**, and **have compassion** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [I will show them no mercy at all]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative expression **so as not to destroy them**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and I will have no compassion, but I will surely destroy them] or [and I will have no compassion that would cause me to preserve them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **compassion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will not act compassionately]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **destroy**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [so as to preserve them]

15.note: The verbs **Listen**, **give ear**, and **be proud** are plural here because Jeremiah is addressing the people of Judah, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The terms **Listen** and **give ear** mean similar things. Jeremiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Listen very carefully]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **proud**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [be humble]
Here, **ear** represents paying attention. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and pay attention]

16.note: Jeremiah is using **Give glory to Yahweh your God** as a common expression of the culture to mean “honor Yahweh your God.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Show honor to Yahweh your God]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the disaster that Yahweh will bring on the people were **darkness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before he brings a time of disaster]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the ruin that will come on the people were their **feet** stumbling on mountain paths in the dark. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he brings ruin on you while you are helpless in the growing dark]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the deliverance that the people hope for were **light**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you hope for deliverance]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [but he turns it into utterly gloomy darkness]

17.note: Jeremiah is presenting a possible condition, that the people of Judah will refuse to listen to what Yahweh says. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [But suppose you refuse to listen. Then my soul will weep in secret places]
Here, **my soul** represents I myself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I myself will weep]

Jeremiah is using **in secret places** as a common expression of the culture to mean “where no one else can see.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [where no one can see me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **pride**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your proud behavior]
The pronoun **she** refers to the soul of Jeremiah, which he mentions earlier in the verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and my soul will weep bitterly]

Jeremiah is repeating forms of the verb **weep** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [and she will weep bitterly]

The expression **has been taken captive** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [enemies have taken Yahweh’s flock captive]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of Judah were a **flock** of sheep that belongs to Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s people have been taken captive]

18.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Tell the king and to the queen mother to make themselves low, sit down]

The words “The Lord told me” are not in the text but are implied. This is the beginning of what Yahweh said to Jeremiah. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh said,]

Coming down from the throne and sitting on the ground was a symbolic action by which a king and a queen mother showed that they had been humbled and were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Come down from your thrones and sit on the ground to show that you are humbled and mourning]

The phrase **Make low! Sit!** expresses a single idea. The word **Make low** tells more about **Sit**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [Come down and sit humbly in the dust]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the crown of your glory** before the information about what has happened to it. Alternate translation: [for the crown of your glory has come down from your heads]
Here, **crown** represents royal authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your glorious royal authority]

19.note: The implication is that enemy armies will besiege these cities so that no one can go in or out of them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The cities of the Negev are shut up by besieging armies, and no one can pass in or out of them]

The expression **are shut up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Enemies have shut up the cities of the Negev]

The expressions **has been exiled** and **has been wholly exiled** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Enemies have carried away all of Judah, they have carried her away completely]

In this verse, the word **Judah** is singular in form, and Yahweh refers back to it with the singular pronoun **she**, but it refers to all of the people of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “Judah” and a plural pronoun. Alternate translation: [have been exiled, they have been wholly exiled]

20.note: The word **your** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing the people of Jerusalem, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using **Lift up your eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “look.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Look and see]

The implication is that **the ones coming from the north** are enemy armies that will invade the land. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the invading armies that are coming from the north]

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the leaders of Jerusalem for failing to care for the people whom he entrusted to them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have lost the flock given to you, your beautiful flock!]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were a **flock** of sheep that he had entrusted to their leaders. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people entrusted to you, your beautiful people]

The expression **given to you** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the flock that God gave to you]

21.q: מַה־תֹּֽאמְרִי֙ כִּֽי־יִפְקֹ֣ד עָלַ֔יִ⁠ךְ וְ֠⁠אַתְּ לִמַּ֨דְתְּ אֹתָ֥⁠ם עָלַ֛יִ⁠ךְ אַלֻּפִ֖ים לְ⁠רֹ֑אשׁ
21.note: Yahweh is using the question form to warn the people of Judah about what is going to happen to them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You will have nothing to say when he appoints over you those friends whom you, yourself, have taught, to be head over you!]

The pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) Yahweh, who will set foreign rulers over the people of Judah. Alternate translation: [the Lord sets over you] or (2) the enemy ruler who will appoint officials to rule over them. Alternate translation: [they set as head over you]

21.q: עָלַ֔יִ⁠ךְ וְ֠⁠אַתְּ לִמַּ֨דְתְּ אֹתָ֥⁠ם עָלַ֛יִ⁠ךְ אַלֻּפִ֖ים לְ⁠רֹ֑אשׁ
21.note: The implication is that the nations whom the people of Judah had cultivated as allies will become the rulers over them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [over you those whom you yourself taught to be your friends, making them rulers over you]
Here, **head** represents ruler. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to be ruler]

21.q: הֲ⁠ל֤וֹא חֲבָלִים֙ יֹאחֱז֔וּ⁠ךְ כְּמ֖וֹ אֵ֥שֶׁת לֵדָֽה
21.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that great anguish will certainly come upon the people of Judah. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Surely labor pains will seize you like a woman in labor!]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a woman in labor** suffers sudden and severe pain, so the people of Judah will suffer great anguish. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [suddenly and severely, causing you great anguish]

22.note: Yahweh is using **say in your heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “think to yourself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And if you ask yourself]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And when you ask yourself why these things have come upon you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Because you have sinned so much]

The expressions **have been uncovered** and **have been exposed** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [your enemies have uncovered your skirts and exposed your heels]
